Please cite these materials as: Sharma, T., Ihle, M., & Von Grebmer Zu Wolfsthurn, S. (2026). *Running simulations and power analysis in R* [Quarto slides]. [LMU Open Science Center](https://www.osc.lmu.de/). [https://lmu-osc.github.io/teaching-material-for-novices/open-research-tools/simulations](https://lmu-osc.github.io/teaching-material-for-novices/open-research-tools/simulations)
:::

**Welcome!** This workshop is intended to **introduce** the **principles and practical use of simulations** in research using **R**. Learners will first get familiar with **what simulations are** and **why they are widely used** in scientific research, including how they help researchers explore statistical behavior, test assumptions, and design studies before collecting real data. The workshop will also **introduce power analysis**, explaining how to **determine appropriate sample sizes** for experiments. Through a subsequent self-paced practical tutorial, learners will work through the **full simulation workflow in R**, including generating random data, repeating simulations, and analyzing results.

### Who are these materials for?

- **Educators** in higher education with or without familiarity with open research planning to **teach open research novices**
- **Self-learners** with no or limited familiarity with open research planning to **develop and build** up on their open research skills

### Prerequisites

<div style="font-size: 0.8em;">
| Prerequisite   |  Description  | Link/Where to find it   |
|------------|------------|------------|
| R and RStudio installed | Latest versions of both R and RStudio | [Download RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) |
| R basics | e.g., how to select a value in a data frame, how to create a vector | [OSC tutorial link](https://lmu-osc.github.io/introduction-to-R/) |
| Familiarity with basic statistical concepts | e.g., hypothesis testing, descriptive statistics, data analysis | [Cheatsheet Link](assets/cheatsheet.pdf) |
</div>

### Learning objectives

At the end of this session, you or your learners will be able to ...

- **Understand** the concept of simulations
- **Explain** the purpose of simulations in research
- **Summarize** how simulations support hypothesis testing and experimentation
- **Perform** the simulation process in the context of a fictional experiment
- **Understand** the concept of power analysis
- **Explain** the purpose of power analysis in research
- **Summarize** how power analysis supports hypothesis testing and experimentation
- Successfully **perform** a simulation in R
